hook: Pour 1 mL of strong acid into a glass of water and its pH drops by five units. Pour the same acid into a glass of acetate buffer and the pH barely moves, by less than a tenth. Nothing magic happens: the acid is still added, but particles in the buffer react with it before it can pile up.

prereq.why: A weak acid and its conjugate base; HNO₂ is weak.

prereq.q: For an acid with pKa 4.7, which form predominates at pH 5.7?
prereq.why: pH is 1 unit above pKa, so [A⁻]/[HA] = 10.

figure.caption: The same 0.010 mol of hydroxide changes the buffer's pH by 0.09 units and pure water's by 5.00.

chain.cause: Strong acid is added to a buffer
chain.effect: H₃O⁺ + A⁻ → HA + H₂O runs to completion, so the added H₃O⁺ does not stay free

chain.cause: Strong base is added to a buffer
chain.effect: OH⁻ + HA → A⁻ + H₂O runs to completion, so the added OH⁻ does not stay free

chain.cause: Each addition only shifts a little HA into A⁻ or back
chain.effect: the ratio [A⁻]/[HA] changes slightly, so [H₃O⁺] = Ka × [HA]/[A⁻] changes slightly

chain.cause: Diluting a buffer lowers [HA] and [A⁻] by the same factor
chain.effect: the ratio, and so the pH, stays almost the same

ideas: Buffer action: added acid is consumed by A⁻; added base is consumed by HA. The added ion is turned into a member of the pair.
Buffer pH depends on the ratio [A⁻]/[HA], not on the amounts. Same ratio, same pH.
Diluting a buffer barely changes its pH.
A buffer limits pH change; it does not stop it. Each addition shifts the ratio a little.

misconception.wrong: A more concentrated buffer has a lower pH because it contains more acid.
misconception.right: It also contains more conjugate base. The pH depends on the ratio [A⁻]/[HA], so two buffers with the same ratio have the same pH; the concentrated one can simply absorb more added acid or base.

summary: A buffer resists pH change because its two components react with whatever is added: the conjugate base takes up added acid and the weak acid takes up added base. Only the ratio [A⁻]/[HA] sets the pH, so additions shift it slightly and dilution barely at all.
